turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CAREGIVER): She's been miserable with that pee again, Doctor. Up and down all night. I finally got her in the car.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Burning when you urinate?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. It burns. Real bad at the end.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Um... four days? Thursday, I think. Or maybe—
[SEG0006] person_1 (CAREGIVER): No, she was already complaining last week. Two weeks, I'd say. She just won't—
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I can't put a date on it. It comes and goes in my head.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): So we'll call it somewhere between four days and two weeks. Not settled.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): And it burns every single time I go. Like every hour. Sometimes I barely get to the bathroom.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood in the urine?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I checked. Maybe a little cloudy. I don't know.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever? Chills?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever. I don't feel chilled.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain in the back, either side, up high?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No. It's down low. An ache, right over the bladder. Not the back.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nausea or vomiting?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many times this year?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): This is the third time this year. Well, actually... maybe the fourth. I lose track. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Antibiotics from us each time?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): They gave me something. I never remember the name. Last time they said the urine was borderline. Not a real infection, they said, but not clean either.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Culture, or just the dipstick?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Nobody gave me a number. Just "borderline."
[SEG0024] person_1 (CAREGIVER): And she already took pills this week. Her sister's leftovers. I told her not to.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): You took your sister's antibiotic?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Just a few. Those brown and yellow capsules, the bladder ones. She had them from her own water infection. I thought if I just—
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): The name.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Macrobid. No— wait. I don't actually know the name. They were just brown and yellow. I shouldn't have said Macrobid.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many, and for how long?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): I took those brown and yellow ones for this burning. One capsule twice a day, I think. I don't know the milligrams, doctor. Not two hundred, that was a guess.
[SEG0031] person_1 (CAREGIVER): She told me five days this morning. Then she counted the foil. Three days, and they ran out yesterday.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. Three days. They're gone.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Other daily medicines?
[SEG0034] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Don't let her start on the sister's bottle again. That's not hers.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Just the water tablet. Sorry.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hydrochlorothiazide?

[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): That's the one, my water tablet. Twelve and a half... no, twenty-five milligrams, and I swallow it every morning for my pressure. Most mornings, though I miss one sometimes. I don't know, doctor, not on purpose.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else? Sugar tablets?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Just that water tablet.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I'm not allergic to anything.
[SEG0042] person_1 (CAREGIVER): That's not what she told me. Sulfa, Bactrim, gave her hives a few years back. She said she stays away from it.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I don't remember any hives. I really don't.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then sulfa stays possible. I won't use it today. Any vaginal discharge?
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. I'm fine.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Itching, sores, odor?
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Can we not do this part.
[SEG0048] person_1 (CAREGIVER): She was scratching in the car. I saw her.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): It's embarrassing. I don't want to talk about—
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes or no. Itching?

[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): A little itching for a couple of days, and I don't know if it's even related. Not really discharge. Well... maybe a tiny bit of white stuff, I don't know, doctor. It's not much.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain with intercourse?
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm not— no. Not recently. Can we move on.
[SEG0054] person_1 (CAREGIVER): She's widowed. Agency sends me days. Nights she's on her own. That's the setup.
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Diabetes? Kidney problems?
[SEG0056] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Pressure is the only thing. Been years.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): So hypertension, we already know that.
[SEG0058] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Her mother had bladder infections all the time. And sugar, near the end.
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): Surgeries?
[SEG0060] person_3 (PATIENT): Appendix out, when I was a kid. Nothing else I remember. I don't know, doctor, I don't think there's more.
[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): Smoke?
[SEG0062] person_3 (PATIENT): Never.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0064] person_3 (PATIENT): A glass of wine, maybe once a week. Not much.
[SEG0065] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lie back. I'm pressing on your abdomen.
[SEG0066] person_2 (DOCTOR): Soft. Tender just above the pubic bone. Flanks are not tender.
[SEG0067] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow. Yeah, that's the spot. Sorry.
[SEG0068] person_2 (DOCTOR): Urine today. Dipstick and a culture. Both.
[SEG0069] person_3 (PATIENT): I just went before we came in. I don't know if I can go again.
[SEG0070] person_2 (DOCTOR): Drink water in the waiting room. The desk has the cup. We'll collect it before you leave.
[SEG0071] person_1 (CAREGIVER): Are you giving her a real antibiotic this time? Those leftovers did nothing.

[SEG0072] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not a treatment antibiotic until the urine is back. No sulfa regardless. I will send phenazopyridine, by mouth, two hundred milligrams three times a day, for two days only. It numbs the burning and the urine turns orange.
[SEG0073] person_3 (PATIENT): The orange pee pills? I had those once. Okay.
[SEG0074] person_2 (DOCTOR): Prescription goes to your pharmacy. Do not take any more of your sister's capsules. Not one.
[SEG0075] person_3 (PATIENT): I won't. They're gone anyway.
[SEG0076] person_1 (CAREGIVER): And if tonight is as bad as last night?

[SEG0077] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it's not settling in three days after we have a result, come back sooner. Same if you get fever, vomiting, or pain up in the back. Either way I want a visit in one week to go over the culture.
[SEG0078] person_3 (PATIENT): A week. I don't know, doctor, rides are hard.
[SEG0079] person_1 (CAREGIVER): I'll get her here. I can swap my Thursday with the agency. Don't worry about that part.
[SEG0080] person_2 (DOCTOR): Most likely another bladder infection. Cystitis. I can't name the germ until the culture, and the itch means a vaginal irritation isn't off the table.
[SEG0081] person_3 (PATIENT): So it might not even be the bladder? I don't know what to think.
[SEG0082] person_2 (DOCTOR): Drink water, don't hold it, and skip the leftover pills. That's the plan.
[SEG0083] person_3 (PATIENT): Alright. Thanks. Sorry I was... you know. Embarrassed.
[SEG0084] person_2 (DOCTOR): Don't be. Give the sample on your way out.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
